provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Abraham trusted God
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the story of Abraham.
The pupils should be able to explain trust in God.

Introduction:
We have learned about God's creation.
Today we learn about Abraham who trusted God.

Content:
Abraham was a man who loved God.
God told Abraham to leave his home.
Abraham trusted God and moved to a new land.
God promised Abraham many children.
Like when a parent gives money for school.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw Abraham following God.

Evaluation questions:
Who did God call?
What did God promise Abraham?
How can we show trust in God?

Summary:
Abraham trusted God completely.

topics.title: God keeps His promises
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list God's promises to Abraham.
The pupils should be able to explain how God keeps promises.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about Abraham trusting God.
Today we see how God kept His promise to Abraham.

Content:
God promised Abraham a son named Isaac.
Abraham and Sarah waited many years.
Even when they were old God kept His promise.
Isaac was born just as God said.
Like when mama says she will buy you new shoes.

Class activity:
Pupils will act out the story of Isaac's birth.

Evaluation questions:
What was God's promise to Abraham?
What was the promised child's name?
Can God do what He says?

Summary:
God always keeps His promises to us.

topics.title: Jacob and his family
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify Jacob's twelve sons.
The pupils should be able to explain God's big family.

Introduction:
We learned about Isaac who was promised by God.
Today we learn about Jacob and his many sons.

Content:
Jacob was Isaac's son.
Jacob had twelve sons.
These twelve sons became twelve tribes.
They were God's big family in Israel.
Like when one family has many children in a compound.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw the twelve sons of Jacob.

Evaluation questions:
How many sons did Jacob have?
What did these sons become?
Who is part of God's family?

Summary:
Jacob's family became God's chosen people.

topics.title: Joseph the dreamer
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell Joseph's coat story.
The pupils should be able to explain dreams from God.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about Jacob's big family.
Today we learn about Joseph who loved God.

Content:
Joseph was Jacob's favorite son.
He had a special coat with many colors.
Joseph had dreams from God.
His dreams showed he would be important.
Like when you dream about your future job.

Class activity:
Pupils will color a picture of Joseph's coat.

Evaluation questions:
What did Joseph's father give him?
What did Joseph see in his dreams?
Can God speak to us in dreams?

Summary:
Joseph trusted God even when things were hard.

topics.title: Joseph forgave his brothers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain forgiveness.
The pupils should be able to tell how Joseph forgave.

Introduction:
We learned about Joseph and his special dreams.
Today we learn how Joseph forgave his brothers.

Content:
Joseph's brothers were jealous of him.
They sold Joseph to faraway Egypt.
Joseph became important in Egypt.
When his brothers came Joseph forgave them.
Like when you forgive your friend for breaking your pencil.

Class activity:
Pupils will role-play Joseph forgiving his brothers.

Evaluation questions:
What did Joseph's brothers do to him?
What did Joseph do when he saw them?
Why is forgiveness important?

Summary:
Joseph showed us how to forgive others.

topics.title: Moses: God calls the humble
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the story of the burning bush.
The pupils should be able to explain how God can use them.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about Joseph's forgiveness.
Today we learn about Moses who heard God.

Content:
Moses was taking care of sheep.
He saw a bush burning but not burning up.
God spoke to Moses from the bush.
God told Moses to help His people.
Like when your teacher asks you to help clean the classroom.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw Moses and the burning bush.

Evaluation questions:
What did Moses see in the desert?
Who spoke to Moses from the bush?
How can God use you?

Summary:
God called Moses to do important work.

topics.title: God cares for His people
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain manna from heaven.
The pupils should be able to tell how God provides daily.

Introduction:
We learned about Moses hearing God in the desert.
Today we learn how God cared for His people.

Content:
God's people were hungry in the desert.
God gave them special food called manna.
Every morning fresh manna appeared.
Like when mama brings food every day for the family.

Class activity:
Pupils will pretend to collect manna in the classroom.

Evaluation questions:
What did God give His people to eat?
When did the manna come?
How does God care for us?

Summary:
God provides for all our needs every day.

topics.title: The ten commandments: love God
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list the first commandments.
The pupils should be able to explain how to love God only.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about God's provision in the desert.
Today we learn about God's rules for His people.

Content:
God gave Moses ten special rules.
The first rules are about loving God.
We should not worship other gods.
We should not use God's name in vain.
Like when you only listen to your father's instructions.

Class activity:
Pupils will memorize the first two commandments.

Evaluation questions:
How many commandments did God give?
What is the first commandment?
Why should we love God only?

Summary:
God wants us to love Him with all our hearts.

topics.title: The ten commandments: love others
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how to honour parents.
The pupils should be able to tell how to love neighbours.

Introduction:
We learned about the first commandments last week.
Today we learn about loving others from God's rules.

Content:
The commandments teach us to love people.
We must honour our father and mother.
We should not steal or lie to others.
We must love our neighbours like ourselves.
Like when you share your toys with your friends.

Class activity:
Pupils will make a list of ways to love others.

Evaluation questions:
How should we treat our parents?
What should we not do to others?
Who is our neighbour?

Summary:
God wants us to love all people around us.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall stories from this term.
The pupils should be able to sing songs about God.

Introduction:
This week we will review what we learned all term.
We will also sing songs about our Bible stories.

Content:
We remember Abraham who trusted God.
We recall Joseph who forgave his brothers.
We think about Moses who heard God.
We remember the ten commandments.
Like when you review your notes before exams.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to retell a Bible story.

Evaluation questions:
Who was called by God in the desert?
What did God give His people in the desert?
How many commandments did God give?
Why is forgiveness important?

Summary:
We learned many important stories about God's love.
